content.user_title: Write Clear Cold Email Subject Lines
content.value_statement: Generic subject lines can obscure a relevant outreach message. This skill drafts and critiques concise alternatives using four frameworks and audience-specific notes.
actual_capabilities: Suggest three to five subjects spanning at least two frameworks: pain, curiosity, social proof, and direct.
Use audience, value proposition, outreach goal, and relationship context to guide suggestions.
Apply a seven-word limit and avoid all capitals, emojis, clickbait, and fake reply prefixes.
Rank suggestions by predicted audience fit and explain each choice.
Critique a supplied subject with specific issues and improved alternatives.
Request spam-trigger checks against a local reference list when that list is available.
limitations: The supplied package lacks the referenced spam-trigger list, so complete list-based checks require additional material.
The cited performance PDF is not bundled; its campaign results cannot be verified from the supplied file.
The skill does not send emails, run experiments, or measure opens and replies.
Audience-fit rankings are qualitative suggestions, not guaranteed performance or inbox placement.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sales Outreach
use_cases.description: Generate subjects for a defined prospect audience, value proposition, and meeting request.

use_cases.title: Review Campaign Subjects
use_cases.description: Critique draft subjects for length, relevance, deceptive prefixes, and unsupported claims before selecting test candidates.

use_cases.title: Refine Founder Outreach
use_cases.description: Create concise subjects for prospective customers using a clear offer without inventing customer results.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Your First Subjects
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest five subjects for [audience] about [offer]. Use at least two frameworks, keep each under eight words, and explain the fit.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: generate options from a simple audience and offer.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Subject
prompt_templates.prompt: Critique [subject] for [audience]. Flag length, relevance, clickbait, and fake reply prefixes. Suggest three alternatives using only the facts in [email draft].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review an existing subject before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Match the Outreach Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Audience: [audience]. Value proposition: [value]. Goal: [open, reply, or book]. Relationship: [relationship]. Rank five subjects across multiple frameworks with fit notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: tailor subjects to intent and recipient relationship.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Framework Test Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [draft] and [verified evidence], propose five subjects across all four frameworks. Explain fit and tradeoffs. Do not invent results. Note unavailable spam references.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare evidence-based candidates for a separately managed campaign test.

output_examples.input: Suggest subjects for operations leaders about an approval-tracking service. The email asks for a short meeting and provides no customer results.
output: Pain: Approval delays slowing your team? Notes: Focuses on the stated operational problem.
Curiosity: A different approach to approval tracking. Notes: Introduces the offer without claiming measured results.
Direct: Discuss approval tracking next week? Notes: Makes the meeting request explicit.

output_examples.input: Critique this subject for a first outreach email: Re: GUARANTEED RESULTS FOR YOUR TEAM TODAY
output: Issues: The fake reply prefix suggests a prior conversation. All capitals and guaranteed results weaken credibility.
Alternative: A question about your approval process. Reason: Connects to a specific topic without unsupported promises.
Alternative: Discuss your approval workflow? Reason: States a clear, relevant request.
Spam check: The referenced trigger list is unavailable, so a complete list-based check was not performed.

best_practices: Provide the audience, value proposition, outreach goal, and recipient relationship before requesting suggestions.
Use only verified customer evidence and authentic personalization in social-proof subjects.
Provide the spam-trigger reference when available, then test candidates using your own campaign measurements.
anti_patterns: Inventing customer results, recipient details, or previous conversations to make a subject more persuasive.
Using all capitals, emojis, clickbait, or fake Re: and Fwd: prefixes.
Treating qualitative rankings as measured reply rates or guaranteed delivery outcomes.

faq.question: Which subject-line frameworks does the skill use?
faq.answer: It uses pain, curiosity, social proof, and direct frameworks. Suggestions normally span at least two families.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your audience, value proposition, desired action, and recipient relationship. An email draft can supply additional context.

faq.question: Can it critique an existing subject?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies issues and suggests alternatives with reasons for each change.

faq.question: Does it check for spam-trigger words?
faq.answer: It requests checks against a referenced local list. That list is absent from this package, so complete list-based checking requires additional material.

faq.question: Does it guarantee higher reply rates?
faq.answer: No. It provides qualitative fit notes, not measured predictions. The externally cited performance PDF is not included.

faq.question: Does the skill send emails or contact the linked service?
faq.answer: No. It provides writing guidance and a reference link, without instructions to send emails or automatically contact the external service.
